newsitem.title: GERMANY: GOLF-MONTY OUT OF TPC, SEVE IS IN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-MONTY OUT OF TPC, SEVE IS IN.

text.p: European number one Colin Montgomerie of Scotland withdrew on Tuesday from this week's Tournament Players Championship in Hamburg starting on Thursday "for personal reasons".

Montgomerie's surprise withdrawal came less than 24 hours after he shot the best round of the week in the British PGA Championship at Wentworth, an eight-under-par 64, to take fifth place in the event.
His management company, International Management Group (IMG), said they "could add nothing further" to Montgomerie's short explanation.
Earlier on Tuesday Ryder Cup captain Severiano Ballesteros's manager said he would start in Hamburg despite his withdrawal from the PGA after one round with a recurring back injury.
"Despite his injury I can confirm Seve intends playing in Germany," his manager Roddy Carr said. "He'll see how his back reacts then make a decision about the following week's European Grand Prix."
Following his 64, a day after he soared to a 76, Montgomerie had been looking forward to the Hamburg tournament as part of his buildup for next month's U.S. Open.
He won the European zone of the Andersen Consulting world championship a week ago and had shot 69 in the first two rounds of the PGA before the 76 ended his chance.

His pullout also costs him a good chance of improving his position in his bid for a fifth successful European Order of Merit title. He is currently 17th in the table now led by PGA champion Ian Woosnam, who is not playing in Hamburg.
